summary_rationale: Ajmera Realty & Infra India Ltd possesses a genuine structural margin advantage in its 100-acre legacy Wadala i-Land township (near-zero historical land cost) and a 58-year execution brand (46,000+ homes delivered), which drove 5.1x PAT growth from FY21 (₹31 Cr) to FY26 (₹157 Cr) alongside record FY26 pre-sales of ₹1,701 Cr and collections of ₹1,103 Cr. On-balance-sheet debt improved via a ₹225 Cr preferential equity raise in FY25 and debt paydown to ₹646 Cr (0.44x D/E) by September 2026, earning a reaffirmed Crisil A-/Stable rating on August 4, 2026. However, the business remains inherently cyclical, working-capital-intensive, and exposed to newly audited footnote and micro-market risks: 12-year cumulative CFO (₹461 Cr) is only ~53% of cumulative PAT (₹870 Cr), 3-year average ROE is a modest 11.9% (ROCE 14.3%), committed receivables coverage of balance construction costs stepped down to 82% (vs. 100% previously), consolidated contingent liabilities surged to ₹456.89 Cr in FY26 (~31% of net worth, including a ₹125 Cr associate corporate guarantee), CRISIL flags ₹1,465 Cr of planned incremental debt alongside a ₹500 Cr NCD enabling approval, and the 60% Bahrain subsidiary carries a qualified FY26 audit opinion. Inside Wadala East, unlisted Dosti Eastern Bay (~₹44,700/sq ft) and Raymond Realty (~₹34,550/sq ft) create a two-sided pricing pincer around Manhattan (~₹39,500/sq ft), while Kanjurmarg freehold conversion slippage and an 86% H2 FY27 pre-sales hurdle (₹307 Cr booked in H1 vs. ₹2,200 Cr guidance) keep execution on close watch.
